title: Music service chips: label-in-name follow-ups from the RF-173 review
acceptance: The word break between a chip's service name and its state no longer rests on a space-only JSX text node a reflow could drop: a sturdier separator, or no aria-label, with a unit test that fails if the visible text runs the two together.
The reconnect chip's busy state ('Reconnecting…') keeps its visible text inside its accessible name, or the record says why the disabled state is exempt.
The expired-chip branch reuses the shared chip shell classes instead of copying them, and drops the aria-label that only repeats its visible text.
